    What I build

    Websites, web apps
    and custom tools.

    1. 01

      AI products

      Tools where the model does real work: mapping a decision (Plot), product photos with a verification pass (Ditto), and sound from a scene description (SceneSound).

    2. 02

      Web apps and websites

      Focused front ends with personality. Dashboards like ShipZen and Rewind, landing pages, and everything in between.

    3. 03

      Onchain apps

      Smart contracts with a usable interface: invoice factoring (Vault30), payment matching (Recon), proxy voting (Franchisa) and group payments (Collect).

    4. 04

      Three.js and browser games

      Interactive 3D that runs in a tab: an ink painting horror game (Sumi), a graveyard roguelite (Vandal), a red string corkboard (Redstring), and this rooftop.

    5. 05

      Developer tools

      Tools for people who build things: data history with visual diffs (Rewind), focus sessions (ShipZen) and a security demo that makes a revocation gap visible (REVOKED).

    6. 06

      Your little frustration

      Most of my projects started as an annoyance that deserved a tool. If something in your day keeps bugging you, that is a good brief.

    About

    Still learning.
    Always building.

    i’m SAVAGE 愛 — an anime lover who turns “someone should build this” into another project.

    i got into building out of curiosity. now i make tools that solve little frustrations, test weird ideas, and occasionally become something bigger than i planned.

    i’m learning as i go: building, breaking things, figuring out why, and coming back with a better version.

    the goal? make useful stuff that feels good to use. preferably with some personality.

    Questions

    Good to know.

    Ask me directly
    What kind of projects do you take on?

    Websites, web apps and custom tools. That covers AI products, onchain apps, Three.js experiences and browser games. The work above shows the range.

    Which stack do you use?

    TypeScript, React and Next.js for most front ends, Three.js for 3D, Tailwind CSS for styling, Solidity for contracts, and whichever AI models fit the job.

    Can I see the code?

    Yes. Every featured project links to its public repository, and all 63 projects are on GitHub.

    Are the screenshots real?

    Yes. Each preview is captured from the project’s actual public front end. The two games show their title screens. Recon, Redstring and REVOKED have no confirmed public demo, so they link to source only. Some onchain projects run on testnets, and their descriptions say so.

    What is the 3D hideout?

    The same portfolio, built as an interactive Three.js rooftop. Projects live on the workstation, the about page is a journal, and contact is a pocket radio. There is also a cat. It runs best on a laptop or desktop.

    How do we get started?

    Send a short brief with the form below, or reach out by email, X or Telegram. Share the goal, how things work today and your timeline.
